assignedReviews.card_evidence: This distributes the gravitational pull evenly to protect your spine from painful injuries.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gravity and its effect on the body, but it does not teach that gravity is a non-contact force or how it affects materials/objects in predictable ways. It is a practical safety tip about backpack use, not direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en: Always use both shoulder straps for heavy backpacks! This distributes the gravitational pull evenly to protect your spine from painful injuries.
copy.tl: Laging gamitin ang dalawang shoulder straps sa mabigat na backpack! Pantay ang hatak ng gravity para iwasan ang masakit na spine injuries.
copy.bis: Kanunay gamita ang duha ka shoulder straps sa bug-at nga backpack! Patas ang pull sa gravity aron malikayan ang masakit nga spine injuries.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it fills the tiny pores and cracks between soil and rock particles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities using simple equipment to compare different types of soil including sandy, clay, silt, and loam, including comparing the ability of the soils to hold water
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes groundwater occupying pores in soil/rock but does not compare different soil types (sandy, clay, silt, loam) or their water-holding ability, which is the core of G4-E-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Groundwater doesn't flow in underground rivers! Instead, it fills the tiny pores and cracks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of the water cycle in the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions groundwater storage in pores but does not explain the role of the water cycle in the environment, such as evaporation, condensation, precipitation, or how water cycles through ecosystems.

copy.en: Groundwater doesn't flow in underground rivers! Instead, it fills the tiny pores and cracks between soil and rock particles beneath Earth's surface.
copy.tl: Ang groundwater ay hindi dumadaloy sa ilalim ng lupa na parang ilog! Sa halip, pumupuno ito sa maliliit na pores at cracks sa pagitan ng soil at rock particles.
copy.bis: Ang groundwater dili mo-flow ilawom sa yuta sama sa suba! Hinuon, nag-puno kini sa gagmay nga pores ug cracks tali sa soil ug rock particles.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soap molecules break apart the protective fatty outer layer of the virus.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific chemical action of soap on a virus's lipid envelope, but does not describe chemical properties of materials such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable. It shares the chemistry topic but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soap molecules break apart the protective fatty outer layer of the virus.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breaking apart a fatty layer, which loosely relates to breaking bonds, but it does not explain that bond breaking constitutes a chemical change or the formation of a new substance. It does not teach the competency's core concept.

copy.en: Washing hands with soap destroys viruses! Soap molecules break apart the protective fatty outer layer of the virus.
copy.tl: Ang paghuhugas ng kamay gamit ang sabon ay pumapatay ng virus! Binabali ng soap molecules ang proteksiyong taba sa labas ng virus.
copy.bis: Ang paghugas sa kamot gamit ang sabon makaguba sa virus! Ang soap molecules moputol sa protective fatty nga gawas nga layer sa virus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: heat conducts directly from the hot magma below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a real-world example of conduction (heat from magma to rocks), but it does not identify it as advantageous or disadvantageous, nor does it address convection or radiation. It only touches the conduction part of the competency without the required advantage/disadvantage classification.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: heat conducts directly from the hot magma below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions conduction of heat but does not explain the process using the particle model (e.g., particle motion, collisions, energy transfer). It only states that heat conducts, without the particle-level explanation required by the competency.

copy.en:
Ever wondered why rocks near Mount Bulusan feel so hot?

They feel hot because heat conducts directly from the hot magma below!
copy.tl:
Napapaisip ba kung bakit mainit ang mga bato malapit sa Bulkang Bulusan?

Mainit sila kapag hinawakan dahil direktang dumadaloy ang init mula sa magma sa ilalim!
copy.bis:
Nahibawo ba ka ngano init kaayo ang mga bato duol sa Bulkang Bulusan?

Init kaayo sila kung hikapon kay diretso nga nagagikan ang kainit gikan sa magma sa ilawom!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: thermal energy actually flows from the warm drink to the cooler ice!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the direction of thermal energy flow (hot to cold) but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It does not define heat as energy transfer due to temperature difference or contrast heat with temperature as a measure of average kinetic energy. The content is related to heat transfer but does not directly support the competency's skill of explaining the heat-temperature distinction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: thermal energy actually flows from the warm drink to the cooler ice!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that thermal energy flows from warm to cool, which is a general heat-transfer principle, but it does not explain convection or conduction, nor does it use the particle model to describe the underlying processes. No mention of particles, convection currents, or conduction mechanisms. Thus it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Does coldness actually flow into your drink to cool it down?

People often think cold flows in, but thermal energy actually flows from the warm drink to the cooler ice!
copy.tl:
Pumapasok ba talaga ang lamig sa inumin mo para lumamig ito?

Madalas iniisip na malamig ang pumapasok, pero ang thermal energy ay dumadaloy mula sa mainit na inumin papunta sa malamig na yelo!
copy.bis:
Mo-flow ba gyud ang katugnaw padulong sa imong ilimnon aron mapabugnaw?

Kasagaran huna-hunaon nga ang katugnaw mo-flow, pero ang thermal energy mo-flow gikan sa init nga ilimnon paingon sa bugnaw nga ice!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It absorbs heat energy from the liquid!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between heat and temperature
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes heat transfer (absorption) but does not explain the difference between heat and temperature. It does not directly support the competency's skill of distinguishing these concepts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It absorbs heat energy from the liquid!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat absorption but does not explain convection or conduction in terms of the particle model. It lacks the required particle-level explanation of these specific heat transfer processes.

copy.en:
How does an ice cube cool your warm juice?

It absorbs heat energy from the liquid! The ice cube cools your drink by soaking up the heat, not by releasing coldness.
copy.tl:
Paano nagpapalamig ang yelo sa iyong mainit na juice?

Sini-sipsip nito ang heat energy mula sa likido! Nagpapalamig ang yelo sa inumin sa pamamagitan ng pagsipsip ng init, hindi sa paglabas ng lamig.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpalamig sa ice cube sa imong init nga juice?

Nagsuyop kini og heat energy gikan sa likido! Nagpalamig ang ice cube sa imong inuman pinaagi sa pagsuyop sa kainit, dili sa pagpagawas og katugnaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Helium gas is about seven times less dense than the air we breathe
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gas but does not teach the three states of matter (solids, liquids, gases) or their identification. It only uses the word 'gas' in the context of density and floating.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Helium gas is about seven times less dense than the air we breathe
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density and buoyancy, not the particle model (motion, spacing, attraction, temperature effects). No particle-level description is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Helium gas is about seven times less dense than the air we breathe
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe matter as having mass and taking up space. It only refers to a gas and its density, which is not the core concept of this competency.

copy.en:
Why do helium balloons float up in the sky?

Helium gas is about seven times less dense than the air we breathe, so helium balloons float!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang pataas ang mga helium balloon sa langit?

Ang helium gas ay halos pitong beses na mas magaan kaysa sa hangin na ating nilalanghap, kaya lumulutang ang mga helium balloon!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga molutaw pataas ang mga helium balloon sa langit?

Ang helium gas kay mga pito ka beses nga mas ubos ang density kaysa sa hangin nga atong ginhawa, mao nga molutaw ang helium balloons!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Honey is thousands of times more viscous, or resistant to flow, than pure liquid water at room temperature!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires describing the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. The card discusses viscosity (resistance to flow), which is a different property of liquids and does not address shape or volume.

copy.en:
Why is honey so slow to pour?

Honey is thousands of times more viscous, or resistant to flow, than pure liquid water at room temperature!
copy.tl:
Bakit mabagal dumaloy ang honey?

Ang honey ay libu-libong beses mas malapot, o mas matibay sa pagdaloy, kaysa sa purong tubig sa room temperature!
copy.bis:
Nganong hinay mo-flow ang honey?

Ang honey liboan ka beses mas viscous, o mas lisod mo-flow, kaysa sa limpyo nga tubig sa room temperature!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the water vapor in your breath turns into visible fog the moment it hits the chilly air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes condensation of water vapor in breath into fog, which is a change of state, but the competency explicitly requires describing changes of state using diagrams and flowcharts. The card provides no diagram or flowchart, so it does not directly support the required representation.

copy.en: On a cold morning, the water vapor in your breath turns into visible fog the moment it hits the chilly air.
copy.tl: Kapag humihinga ka palabas sa malamig na umaga, nagiging usok ang tubig sa hininga mo dahil nagko-condense ito.
copy.bis: Kung mogawas ka og hangin sa bugnaw nga buntag, ang tubig sa imong pagginhawa mo-condense ug mahimong klarong hamog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: solid water ice is less dense than its liquid form
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density differences between solid and liquid water, not the properties of shape and volume for solids, liquids, and gases. It does not describe definite/indefinite shape or volume, so it does not directly support G5-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: solid water ice is less dense than its liquid form
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions solid and liquid states but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or explicitly state that matter exists in three states. The focus is on density, not on the existence of three states.

copy.en:
Why do ice cubes float in your drink?

Unlike most things, solid water ice is less dense than its liquid form, making those ice cubes float!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang mga ice cube sa iyong inumin?

Kakaiba sa karamihan, ang solid water ice ay less dense kaysa sa liquid form niya, kaya lumulutang ang mga ice cube!
copy.bis:
Nganong molutaw ang mga ice cube sa imong ilimnon?

Lahi sa kadaghanan, ang solid water ice kay less dense kaysa sa liquid form, mao nga molutaw ang mga ice cube!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Its adult stage lasts only twenty-four hours
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the mayfly's short adult life but does not use a flow chart or compare the different stages of an animal life cycle as required by the competency. It is only tangentially related to life cycles.

copy.en:
What's the shortest-lived insect?

The mayfly! Its adult stage lasts only twenty-four hours, the shortest of any insect in the world.
copy.tl:
Alin ang insektong pinakamaikli ang buhay?

Ang mayfly! Dalawampu't apat na oras lang ang buhay ng adult nito, ang pinakamaikli sa lahat ng insekto sa mundo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang insekto nga pinakamubo ug kinabuhi?

Ang mayfly! Baynte kwatro ka oras ra ang kinabuhi sa adult niini, ang pinakamubo sa tanang insekto sa kalibutan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it leaves its barbed stinger stuck in your skin
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the honeybee's stinger, an outer body part, but its role (injecting venom for defense) is not about moving or gathering food, which are the specific roles named in the competency. The competency focuses on head, legs, or wings and their roles in movement and food gathering.

copy.en: When a honeybee stings you, it leaves its barbed stinger stuck in your skin, still pumping venom in even after the bee is gone.
copy.tl: Kapag sinaksak ka ng honeybee, iniiwan nito ang barbed stinger sa balat mo na patuloy na nagbubuga ng lason.
copy.bis: Kung mosakit ka sa honeybee, magbilin kini og barbed stinger sa imong panit nga magpadayon og pump sa venom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The strong winds of a typhoon carry powerful mechanical energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions mechanical energy carried by wind but does not describe kinetic energy as movement of objects/particles or potential energy as stored energy. It only gives an example of moving air having energy, without teaching the required definitions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The strong winds of a typhoon carry powerful mechanical energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the mechanical energy of an object is the sum of the kinetic energy and the potential energy available to do work
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the term 'mechanical energy' but does not explain that it is the sum of kinetic and potential energy available to do work. It does not directly support the competency's explanation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The strong winds of a typhoon carry powerful mechanical energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that energy is something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to energy causing change (uprooting trees) but does not identify energy as something that can cause change including light, sound, and heat energy. It only gives a wind example, not the required general concept or the listed forms.

copy.en: The strong winds of a typhoon carry powerful mechanical energy — enough to uproot banana trees!
copy.tl: Ang malalakas na hangin ng bagyo ay may kinetic energy na kayang hilahin pababa ang mga puno ng saging!
copy.bis: Ang kusog nga hangin sa bagyo adunay kinetic energy nga makapahukay sa mga saging!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A 2-meter crowbar with the fulcrum 0.5 meters from a rock gives a mechanical advantage of three
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out fair tests to show how levers can be used to change the magnitude and direction of a force
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents a single mechanical advantage calculation for a lever, but the competency requires carrying out fair tests to show how levers change the magnitude and direction of a force. No fair test, replication, or direction change is addressed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A 2-meter crowbar with the fulcrum 0.5 meters from a rock gives a mechanical advantage of three
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives one example of a lever's advantage (mechanical advantage), but does not demonstrate advantages and limitations of simple machines through guided investigation, nor does it compare levers with other simple machines or discuss limitations.

copy.en:
Can a crowbar really help you lift 3x more weight?

Yes! A 2-meter crowbar with the fulcrum 0.5 meters from a rock gives a mechanical advantage of three, so you lift three times more weight!
copy.tl:
Kaya bang magbuhat ng tatlong beses na bigat gamit ang crowbar?

Oo! Ang 2-meter na crowbar na may fulcrum na 0.5 meters mula sa bato ay nagbibigay ng mechanical advantage na tatlo, kaya tatlong beses ang mabubuhat mo!
copy.bis:
Makapahakot ba ka og three times nga timbang gamit ang crowbar?

Oo! Ang 2-meter nga crowbar nga ang fulcrum 0.5 meters gikan sa bato naghatag og mechanical advantage nga three, mao nga three times ang imong mabakot!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It travels at exactly 299,792 kilometers per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states the speed of light but does not describe wave properties using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, or velocity. It does not support the skill of identifying how wave properties are described.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How fast does light travel in a vacuum?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a speed value for light but does not identify the general concept that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed. It is a specific fact about light, not instruction on the definition of speed.

copy.en:
How fast does light travel in a vacuum?

It travels at exactly 299,792 kilometers per second, circling the Earth's equator about 7.5 times in just one second!
copy.tl:
Gaano kabilis maglakbay ang light sa isang vacuum?

Naglalakbay ito nang eksaktong 299,792 kilometers per second, kaya napapalibot nito ang equator ng mundo ng halos 7.5 beses sa isang segundo!
copy.bis:
Unus ka paspas moulakaw ang light sa usa ka vacuum?

Moulakaw kini og eksaktong 299,792 kilometers per second, mao nga makalibot kini sa equator sa kalibutan mga 7.5 ka beses sa usa ka segundo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because the material reflects car headlights directly back to the driver!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes retroreflection from reflective tape, an everyday application of light reflection, but the competency specifically requires guided investigations describing and illustrating reflection using plane and curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. The card does not involve mirrors, refraction, or any investigation, so it only shares the broad topic of light reflection.

copy.en:
Why does wearing reflective tape at night make you visible?

Because the material reflects car headlights directly back to the driver!
copy.tl:
Bakit nakikita ka kapag nagsuot ng reflective tape sa gabi?

Dahil nire-reflect ng materyal ang car headlights diretso pabalik sa driver!
copy.bis:
Nganong makita ka kung magsul-ob ug reflective tape sa gabii?

Kay ang material nag-reflect sa car headlights diretso balik sa driver!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light bends when it enters water because it slows down!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains refraction with a straw-in-water everyday example, but the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. No investigation or specified apparatus is present, so it only shares the topic of refraction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Light bends when it enters water because it slows down!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how light behaves (bends/refracts) in an everyday situation, which overlaps with exploring how light behaves. However, the competency focuses on guided science activities to explore sources of light, behavior, and uses; the card is a single explanation without guided activity or exploration, and does not address sources or uses.

copy.en:
Why does a straw look broken in a glass of water?

Light bends when it enters water because it slows down! This makes a partially submerged straw look broken.
copy.tl:
Bakit mukhang naputol ang straw sa loob ng basong may tubig?

Yumuyuko ang light pagpasok sa tubig dahil bumabagal ito! Kaya mukhang naputol ang straw na bahagyang nakalubog.
copy.bis:
Nganong murag naputol ang straw sa sulod sa baso nga may tubig?

Mokurot ang suga pag-sulod sa tubig kay hinay-hinay kini! Mao nga murag naputol ang straw nga medyo nasulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A typical lightning bolt carries about 300 million volts!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that electricity is a flow of electrons and show appreciation for the need to observe safe measures in handling electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a voltage comparison for lightning but does not address electricity as a flow of electrons, nor does it teach safe handling of electricity. It shares the broad topic of electricity but provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A typical lightning bolt carries about 300 million volts!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate the effects of static electricity using common materials, such as a comb, plastic and glass rods, and balloons
assignedReviews.reason: Lightning is a static electricity phenomenon, but the card only states a voltage figure and does not involve investigating effects of static electricity with common materials such as a comb, rods, or balloons. No direct support for the investigation skill.

copy.en: A typical lightning bolt carries about 300 million volts! That is over 1.3 million times stronger than the 230 volts in a standard Philippine wall outlet.
copy.tl: Ang karaniwang kidlat ay may humigit-kumulang 300 milyong volts! Ito ay higit 1.3 milyong beses na mas malakas kaysa sa 230 volts sa karaniwang saksakan sa Pilipinas.
copy.bis: Ang kasagarang kidlat kay nagdala ug mga 300 milyong volts! Kini sobra 1.3 milyong ka beses nga mas kusog kaysa sa 230 volts nga naa sa ordinaryong saksakan sa Pilipinas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The moon has its own gravitational pull! That's why a spacesuit weighs only one-sixth of its Earth weight there.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies gravity as a force and shows it affects weight, but the competency specifically requires gravity's effects on Earth. The card is about the Moon, so it does not directly support the Earth-focused competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The moon has its own gravitational pull! That's why a spacesuit weighs only one-sixth of its Earth weight there.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a weight difference due to gravity but does not describe the effect of gravity on the motion of an object. It addresses weight, not motion, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: The moon has its own gravitational pull! That's why a spacesuit weighs only one-sixth of its Earth weight there.
copy.tl: May sariling gravitational pull ang buwan! Kaya ang spacesuit ay tumitimbang lamang ng isang-anim na bahagi ng bigat nito sa Earth kapag nandoon.
copy.bis: Ang buwan adunay kaugalingong gravitational pull! Mao nga ang spacesuit mobug-at lang og usa ka-unom nga bahin sa gibug-aton niini sa Yuta kung naa sa buwan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The strongest continuous magnetic field in a lab reached 45.5 Tesla
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card presents a trivia fact about the strongest lab magnet's field strength, but does not describe properties of magnets or how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials, nor does it involve a guided investigation. It shares the topic of magnets but provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
How strong is the world's strongest lab magnet?

The strongest continuous magnetic field in a lab reached 45.5 Tesla — that's about 9,000 times stronger than a regular fridge magnet!
copy.tl:
Gaano kalakas ang pinakamalakas na magnet sa laboratoryo?

Ang pinakamalakas na continuous magnetic field sa laboratoryo ay umabot ng 45.5 Tesla — mga 9,000 beses na mas malakas kaysa karaniwang magnet sa ref!
copy.bis:
Unsa ka kusog ang pinakakusog nga magnet sa laboratoryo?

Ang pinakakusog nga continuous magnetic field sa laboratoryo nakaabot og 45.5 Tesla — mga 9,000 ka beses nga mas kusog kaysa ordinaryong magnet sa ref!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Never crush or dissolve a time-release medicine pill in water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions dissolving a pill in water but does not demonstrate or explain factors affecting solubility, such as heat, nor does it teach solubility concepts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Never crush or dissolve a time-release medicine pill in water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves dissolving a substance in water but does not identify the roles of solute and solvent in a solution.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Never crush or dissolve a time-release medicine pill in water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate ways to minimize harmful changes in materials, such as restriction of burning of waste materials, and care in handling reactive materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about safe handling of medication, not about minimizing harmful changes in materials such as burning waste or handling reactive materials.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Never crush or dissolve a time-release medicine pill in water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment, such as trash disposal, and burning household materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card warns about a dangerous effect of a medicine, but does not explain how changes in materials can be harmful to living and non-living things in the environment.

copy.en: Never crush or dissolve a time-release medicine pill in water! It makes the medicine enter your body too fast, causing a dangerous overdose.
copy.tl: Huwag durugin o tunawin ang time-release na gamot sa tubig! Pumasok ito nang mabilis sa katawan, na pwedeng magdulot ng delikadong overdose.
copy.bis: Ayaw pagdugmok o pagtunaw og time-release nga tambal sa tubig! Mosulod kini dayon sa lawas, nga mahimong hinungdan sa delikadong overdose.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies mercury as a liquid metal, but does not address fixed chemical composition, elements/compounds, or unique proton numbers, which are the core of G8-M-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
